title: Cut one page out of a list with skip and limit

blocks.text: `skip(n)` drops the first `n` elements and `limit(n)` keeps at most `n`. Together they cut a slice out of a stream, which is exactly what pagination needs. Both take a `long`.

Write `Pager.page(List<Integer> items, int page, int size)`. Pages are numbered from `0` and hold `size` items each; return the items of page `page`, in order. `page` is never negative and `size` is at least `1`.
The list does not always divide into whole pages, a caller may ask past the end, and `page * size` in `int` arithmetic can overflow.

cases.says: It returns the size items of the page asked for, counting pages from 0.
The last page holds whatever is left, even if that is fewer than size items.
A page past the end is empty, not an error: skip past the end leaves an empty stream.
page * size is computed as a long, so a huge page number gives an empty page instead of an overflowed, negative skip.

concepts: skip(n) drops the first n elements and limit(n) keeps at most n, which together cut a page.
